title: beads-bootstrap.sh rm -rf's local engine gated only on a local '0' count — verify recoverability BEFORE deleting
description:
scripts/beads-bootstrap.sh runs automatically every SessionStart (via install-bd.sh). When 'bd stats' reports 0 issues it executes 'rm -rf .beads/embeddeddolt .beads/dolt' and THEN tries 'bd bootstrap' to pull from origin. It never verifies origin actually carries refs/dolt/data before deleting. Combined with Bench-h4f (origin often has no ref), this is a latent data-loss hazard: 'delete, then hope'. (Note: it removes only the engine subdirs and guards on '[ -d .beads ]', so it cannot delete .beads/ wholesale — scope the fix to the engine-clear path.)

Acceptance criteria:
- Invert the order: prove a recovery source exists (origin refs/dolt/data reachable, OR a non-empty committed .beads/issues.jsonl) BEFORE removing any engine dir.
- If neither source exists, refuse to clear and log a loud warning; leave the (possibly cold) local engine intact.
- Red test: with bd stats=0 and origin carrying NO refs/dolt/data and no committed issues.jsonl, the script must NOT rm the engine dirs and must exit non-destructively.

title: bench:init never establishes refs/dolt/data on origin — local-only boards have no rehydrate source
description:
Bench's entire rehydrate model assumes 'reachable Dolt history lives on git origin under refs/dolt/data' (stated in scripts/beads-bootstrap.sh). But nothing in commands/init.md, templates/CLAUDE.bench.md, or any script ever runs 'bd dolt remote add' or 'bd dolt push'. The ONLY code that creates refs/dolt/data is scripts/beads-cloud-push.sh, which is web-only (gated on CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true). Net: a local-only Bench user never gets a portable rehydrate source, so every cold-board bootstrap is an unrecoverable no-op.

Acceptance criteria:
- bench:init Step 2 configures a Dolt remote (origin) and performs an initial 'bd dolt push' so refs/dolt/data exists from day one.
- init verifies .beads/issues.jsonl is COMMITTED (not merely staged).
- A non-web local SessionEnd path keeps origin's refs/dolt/data current (generalize beads-cloud-push.sh or add a local equivalent).
- Red test: a fresh 'bench:init' in a repo with an origin results in 'git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*' returning a ref.

title: doctor/health-check: add RED invariant — destructive bootstrap enabled + no recoverable source
description:
skills/beads-health-check/SKILL.md reads and compares local vs remote refs/dolt/data and can push it, but nothing asserts the dangerous combination that causes loss: destructive bootstrap path enabled AND no recoverable source (no origin refs/dolt/data AND no non-empty committed .beads/issues.jsonl) = RED. bench:doctor likewise just notes the bootstrap hook exists. This check, run against the bench repo's own prior state, would have flagged the exposure before any loss.

Also steer Bench projects OFF the global/shared Dolt engine toward a repo-local engine: the shared server (~/.beads/shared-server) is the component that actually corrupted in the incident, and a shared engine gives a destructive bootstrap cross-project blast radius.

Acceptance criteria:
- beads-health-check emits a RED finding when bootstrap-clear is reachable and no recovery source exists.
- doctor reports global/shared-engine usage as a warning with the repo-local remediation.
- Red test: a repo with a local board, destructive bootstrap enabled, and no origin ref + no committed jsonl produces a RED health-check result.
